correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the two extremes leaves a simple random sample of n-2 points from the r-1 interior lattice sites. The exact interior first moment, second raw moment, and finite-population correction to the sample-sum variance determine E[Q] and E[T^2], hence E[S^2]. The resulting expression is independent of the minimum, so conditioning only on the range is valid. Exhaustive exact-rational enumeration independently checks every range stratum for populations through endpoint 17. The finite enumeration is supplementary; the proof covers all admissible M,n,r.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The continuous result does not imply the lattice theorem: its conditional interior sample is iid continuous uniform after normalization, whereas here the interior points are sampled without replacement from finitely many lattice sites. The different conditional law is exactly what generates the correction.

value.rationale: Range and sample variance are canonical dispersion summaries, and simple random sampling without replacement is the basic finite-population design. Conditioning on an observed range is a natural finite-sample calibration problem. The theorem shows that for an arithmetic population the ambient population size disappears completely after conditioning, while discreteness leaves an exact first-order lattice correction to the continuous-uniform regression. This is a structural finite-population identity rather than a recomputation of a known marginal moment.
